newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks follow Dow to open at new record high.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks follow Dow to open at new record high.

text.p: Australian shares opened at a record high on Monday with investors happy to follow Wall Street's lead after the Dow finished above the 6800 level for the first time on Friday.
At 10.20 a.m. (2320 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 9.9 points at 2,445.4, eclipsing its previous all time high of 2,444.2, which was set on January 15.
The March share price index was up 19 points at 2,463 and at a 17.6 point premium to the underlying index.
Major banks were leading the market, with Commonwealth Bank the most active stock in early trading.
"The market is up on the back of the U.S. market and because there is a rumour that Commonwealth Bank may pay a special dividend," a dealer at a Brisbane-based brokerage said.
At 11.30 a.m. (0030 GMT), Commonwealth Bank shares were 14 cents higher at A$12.70 (US$9.91) after touching a record high of A$12.75.
Other major banks also opened firmer with Westpac up six cents at A$7.21 and National Australia Bank up eight at A$14.91.
The dealer said a key factor emerging for investors was the half year reporting season which starts in February.
Analysts are concerned that weaker earnings could force a reassessment of the market's medium term outlook.
